status: DRAFT, NOT REGISTERED, NOT RUN. Exploration-derived. Needs Erin's go-ahead, then the new kind and its controls, before freezing.
kind: first_sign_rarity (NEW KIND: not yet implemented; needs code in indus_workbench/hypotheses.py plus synthetic positive and negative controls in tests/test_core.py before freezing)

rarity.definition: A sign is RARE if it occurs 5 times or fewer in the EXPLORATION split (damaged dropped, duplicates removed, unidentified dropped), OR does not occur in exploration at all (unseen = rare). Holdout frequencies are never used to decide rarity.
rarity.note: Every sign not in common_signs_frozen is rare. The exploration rare list (371 types) is implied.

params.texts: Holdout texts whose FIRST sign is not an opener (no heading). Trailing closers are removed; the remaining 'middle' must have 3 or more signs.

positions.first: the first sign of the text (= first middle sign), unless it is a numeral (then the text contributes no first-sign observation)
positions.interior: middle signs strictly between the first and the last middle sign, excluding numerals and any opener
positions.last_middle: the sign just before the closers (secondary, descriptive only)

params.statistic: share of first signs that are rare MINUS share of interior signs that are rare
params.null: within each text, the non-numeral middle signs are permuted (keeps each text's signs and length, destroys position); 2,000 permutations
params.secondary_descriptive: report the interior-vs-last-middle contrast too, to show whether the effect is just 'text edges attract rare signs'. Not part of the registered claim.

statement: Among holdout inscriptions that lack a heading, the first sign is a rare sign (rare = 5 or fewer uses in the exploration corpus, or unseen there) more often than the interior middle signs of the same inscriptions are.

expectation_from_exploration.note: The scouting note quoted 19% vs 10%; those used a broader slot definition including numerals. These are the figures for this exact definition.

support_and_power.min_support: 15 first-sign observations (verdict 'Inconclusive' below that); expected about 166
support_and_power.power: about 0.94 if the exploration gap holds (25% vs 14%); about 0.77 if it shrinks by half

multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg across every confirmatory test ever run (this would be the 19th), as in scripts/run_confirmatory.py
how_to_run_later: 1) implement kind 'first_sign_rarity' with controls; 2) freeze with hypotheses.freeze(), save as hypotheses/H-<date>-<sha8>.json, commit and push; 3) python scripts/run_confirmatory.py (once)
